decisions.statement: The reading is the reading the tracking day has for the day asked for.
The surplus a day has is the day's sleep less the day's spend.
A surplus below zero is a reading.
A surplus given as text is read as the number that text spells.
No tracking day is no reading rather than a surplus of zero.
A tracking day with no surplus is no reading rather than a surplus of zero.
A day with neither sleep nor spend is no reading rather than a surplus of zero.
A surplus falls with the clock while a stretch of the day is still running.
How fast it falls is the sum of what an hour of each running stretch costs.
A running stretch whose hour costs nothing has the surplus fall at nothing.
The cost of an hour is read from the one module the day's spend reads it from.
A stretch with no end is the stretch running now.
Nothing here caches a reading or decides when a reading is taken.
Nothing here turns a surplus into a color.

definition: how much of Alan's night the day has left him
